title: Chapter 15
text: CONSEQUENCES Afterward I found under my left shoulder the most curious wound. As though I had leaned against some whirring thing, it bleeds secretly. Nobody knows its name. Afterward, for a reason more right than rational, I thought of that fat German in his ill-fitting overcoat in the woods near Vienna, realizing that the birds were going farther and farther away, and no matter how fast he walked he couldn’t keep up. How does any of us live in this world? One thing compensates for another, I suppose. Sometimes what’s wrong does not hurt at all, but rather shines like a new moon. I often think of Beethoven rising, when he couldn’t sleep, stumbling through the dust and crumpled papers, yawning, settling at the piano, inking in rapidly note after note after note.
